title: Raaka Sets Guinness World Record With 37 Simultaneous Motion-Capture Performers
excerpt: Allu Arjun and Atlee's sci-fi epic was certified by Guinness World Records on September 15 for capturing 37 performers in real time — a first for a film production of this scale.
body:
• Raaka has entered the Guinness World Records for the "Most People Motion-Captured in Real-Time," with 37 performers captured simultaneously in a single session.
  • The session took place in February 2026 and was certified on September 15, 2026, with the certificate presented to Allu Arjun and Atlee in Mumbai.
  • The production used 92 optical motion-capture cameras to capture performers aged 4 to 70 within one volume, with real-time Unreal Engine visualization.
  • The Atlee-directed sci-fi epic, produced by Sun Pictures and co-starring Deepika Padukone, is expected to release in 2027.
Allu Arjun and director Atlee's upcoming film *Raaka* has entered the Guinness World Records for the "Most People Motion-Captured in Real-Time," after 37 performers were captured simultaneously during a single motion-capture session in Mumbai. Guinness certified the record on September 15, 2026, with senior adjudicator Swapnil Dangrikar presenting the official certificate to Allu Arjun and Atlee at a private event attended by the film's production team, according to Bollywood Hungama. The record is officially credited to Sun TV Network Limited and director V. Arunkumar, professionally known as Atlee, for the Allu Arjun-starring film. The technical demands were steep. The 37 performers ranged from a 4-year-old child to a 70-year-old, and every individual performance had to be captured and preserved simultaneously within a single volume. The production deployed 92 optical motion-capture cameras alongside systems for calibration, networking, synchronization, facial capture, witness cameras, and real-time Unreal Engine visualization — a custom pipeline the film's VFX team developed for the project's requirements.

"This achievement would not have been possible without the vision and direction of my director, Mr. Atlee, and the incredible work of the entire team. I would also like to thank Sun Pictures for their constant support and for backing a project of this scale and ambition."

— Allu Arjun

Context & Background

*Raaka* is one of the most anticipated Indian films in production — a science-fiction action epic directed by Atlee and produced by Kalanithi Maran's Sun Pictures, with Allu Arjun in the lead and Deepika Padukone as the female lead. The project pairs the Telugu star, coming off the massive *Pushpa* franchise, with Atlee, whose recent directing work has defined big-canvas commercial Indian cinema. Motion capture has grown central to Indian blockbusters chasing Hollywood-scale VFX, but most productions capture ensembles in batches. Capturing 37 performances live in one volume is a different engineering problem: every camera, sensor, and network sync must hold frame-accuracy across dozens of moving bodies, or the entire take is lost. Real-time Unreal visualization added another layer — directors could see the composite scene render live, rather than waiting for post-production. Early glimpses have already set expectations. The film's first look, released earlier this year, showed Allu Arjun in a striking beast-like appearance, while the makers have kept the story under wraps, according to TradingView's report. Filmmaker Sibi Chakravarti, who viewed early visuals, compared the film's ambition to the work of S.S. Rajamouli, and lyricist Vivek said the visual quality holds up against high-end Hollywood productions, Zoom TV reported.

Impact & Analysis

The Guinness title does double duty for the film. Before a frame of footage has been shown publicly, *Raaka* now carries a certified, globally verifiable proof of its technical scale — a marketing asset that no trailer can buy. Sun Pictures described the achievement as a moment that takes Indian cinema "to the world stage," and the certification gives that claim an objective anchor. The record also signals how far India's VFX infrastructure has come. Building a 92-camera, real-time pipeline in-house is the kind of capability that historically lived in a handful of Hollywood and London facilities. Executing it in Mumbai shows the technical muscle for global-scale spectacle now exists domestically.

"Growing up, we always heard about Guinness World Records with so much wonder, never imagining that one day we would be blessed to achieve one ourselves."

— Atlee, director of Raaka
For Deepika Padukone, the milestone arrives at a personally significant moment. She is part of the film's principal cast and had been working on the project during her pregnancy, with reports indicating she was completing portions of the first installment before taking maternity leave.

Diaspora Angle

For the global Indian audience, *Raaka* is shaping up as a tentpole that competes on craft — the kind of film that pulls diaspora families into theaters on opening weekend the way *RRR* did, with a record story that travels across language barriers.

What's Next

The film is expected to release in 2027, though no official date has been announced. With the Guinness recognition now public, expect the next marketing beats — character reveals, teaser footage, a release-date announcement — to lean on the record as evidence of scale. The real test comes at the box office: whether technological ambition translates into a film audiences embrace.
image_caption: Allu Arjun and director Atlee pose with the Guinness World Records certificate on stage in Mumbai. Their film Raaka set the record for 37 performers in simultaneous motion capture.
